counter_arguments: The PR only updates the `requests` library version; it does not modify any tax‑rate caching logic or the conditions that trigger the cache TTL.
The revisit condition for the workaround is a measurable performance threshold (API latency <200 ms). A dependency bump does not guarantee the tax provider API latency improves to that level.
No changes are made to the `_tax_cache` or `_cache_times` structures, nor to the code that checks `TAX_CACHE_TTL`, so the caching mechanism remains unchanged.
The PR description mentions a security patch, not a performance optimization, and there is no evidence that `requests` 2.32.0 reduces the tax provider’s response time to the required threshold.
Even if the newer `requests` version were marginally faster, the workaround’s condition requires a reliable sub‑200 ms latency, which is far beyond the typical impact of a minor library bump.
The only file changed is `requirements.txt`; no runtime behavior affecting the tax provider calls is altered.
The memory cache workaround was introduced specifically to hide high latency; without addressing the latency itself, the workaround remains necessary.
The workaround HACK-012 is intended to be removed only when the tax provider API latency consistently drops below 200 ms. The PR under review merely bumps the
dependency for a security fix and does not touch any of the caching code
or the API call path. There is no indication that the version change will bring the latency down to the required threshold
nor does it modify the conditions that would make the cache unnecessary. Therefore
the PR does not resolve the underlying condition
and the appropriate verdict is NEEDS_WORK.
